paragraphs: CurbIQ sells curb management software to cities, universities and airports, giving them one place to keep curb regulations and usage data. The problem it addresses is balancing curb access among pedestrians, parking, deliveries, rideshares and vendors.

The platform pulls curb regulation and usage data from multiple sources into a single database. Records are held in curb data standards including CDS, D-TRO and CurbLR. Map overlays show when and where regulations are in effect, and the tool models what a proposed policy change would do. Data sharing runs through APIs so couriers, ride-hailing companies and navigation platforms can see the current rules.

CurbIQ was founded by Peter Richards, formerly chair of the Institute of Transportation Engineers Parking Standing Committee. The team managed the Southern California Association of Governments Curb Space Management Study. The company belongs to the Open Mobility Foundation, a nonprofit that builds open-source tools for cities. CurbIQ itself is a product of the design firm Arcadis.
